newsitem.title: USA: Sinking gold futures drag gold stocks lower.
newsitem.headline: Sinking gold futures drag gold stocks lower.

text.p: Gold stocks fell on Monday as sagging gold futures took some of the luster out of major gold companies, including Newmont Mining Corp, Barrick Gold Corp, ASA Ltd and Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp.

Earlier, gold futures posted fresh life-of-contract lows on the New York commodity exchange in every delivery month out to December 1997. In late trading, they fell even further, with active COMEX December 1996 futures off $2.10 to $374.20 an ounce.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's benchmark index of gold stocks fell 2.22 or 1.85 percent to 117.53. The Standard & Poor's gold index fell $4.30 or 1.79 percent to 236.22.

Salomon gold analyst David Rinhimer said in a research report that gold was off for a number of reasons, including the ferocious rising tide in the equity markets, gaining bonds, and weak seasonal upturn. Reports of soft demand for jewelry and bullion in India during the Hindu festival of lights Diwali have also depressed the outlook, he wrote.
ASA shares lost 3/4 to 37-1/2. Newmont Mining shares fell 3/8 to 48-5/8. Santa Fe shares dropped 1/4 to 11-5/8.
Echo Bay Mines Ltd fell 1/4 to 6-1/2 and Pegasus Gold Inc shares lost 7/8 to 9-1/2, and hit a new 52-week low of 9-3/8. Both were among the most heavily traded issues on the American Stock Exchange.
Other gold stocks that suffered include Golden Star Resources Ltd, off 1-1/2 to 15-1/4; Barrick Gold Corp, falling 1/4 to 27-1/4; and TVX Gold Inc, off 1/8 to 7-1/4.
